I stated before that I would put out a review of Nioh once I got through the game. Well I was hoping to do so before Horizon came out. I didn't. So I am currently up to the .

I have spent 83 hours playing this game on one of my saves. I like grinding and min maxing gear so that is why I am not yet complete with the game. I didn't know there was a NG+ until about 40 hours in. So I have since spent my time working the way to end. This review will contain spoilers which I will not mark outright.

So why did i put "Semi-casual" in the title. Well in regards to dark souls types games I am not the best, nor have I completed the series. I have played some of the first and third. Now, Bloodborne, I have played and I own it along with all the DLC. I haven't completed the DLC yet, pretty hard and side tracked by other games.

What is exactly is Nioh? ~ Nioh is an experience that I would suggest anyone with a PS4 partake and if you don't own a PS4 this might be the title that gets you to buy one. It is a PS4 Exclusive brought to you by the team who created Ninja Gaiden "Team Ninja". The game is set in England and Japan. You are set out on a journey to retrieve an item and save Japan from chaos. The game features a unique combat system with multiple stances, varying weaponry as well as utilities and Magic.

Mission System The game uses a mission based system, different from interlocking games such as Souls and Bloodborne. There is starting point and an end up point with checkpoints along the way. You are then sent to a Map which serves a hub. You can visit a blacksmith, dojo, and additional options that open up after you get past points in the main story. The games map has regions as well which serve as progress system for the story. To progress you most travel to the next region. There are I believe 6 regions in total. (The DLC I belive, will add 3 additional regions or story missions.)

Difficulty: Dark Souls type difficulty. Even the weakest enemy can kill you with the right combo. The streamers even die occasional. The world record holder or 1:25:25:25 Distortion2 died several times in his record breaking play through. So even the worlds best player still dies. Gravity is a killer. Hidden enemies and traps as well. The level design allows for different ways to handle groups, but even the best intentions end in death. The hardest boss for me had to be the second boss in the game, or rather the first real boss you fight. I had to get a player to come in and help me. I have only used the summon twice and both times it was only for the boss after clearing the entire place. Umi Buzo (spelling it wrong) was the other boss. Since then I have gotten a lot better. You know the saying, "Get Gud", well that happened. It will when you spend at least 40 hours. It will take 40 hours at least. The streamer I watched the entire play through of spent like 70 hours.

The patch coming up soon will add PVP and "Harder" missions. How the hell could they make it harder....this was one of the hardest games I have played. I watched a streamer play before I bought it. It looked easy. I get in, and the game is hard, and the streamer made it look so easy. He had beaten every Dark Souls game and provided walkthroughs for it and Bloodborne. SO he was already good.

Co-op: There is co-op, however, until you reach NG+, a friend can only join your mission if they have completed it. You can't play through the main story together. That is done on purpose so that you can't just have the game handed to you. You gain glory which is used for later game stuff. You can also fight remnants. These are the bodies of fallen players. You can activate them and fight their ghost which will drop 1 or more items that player was wearing. Allowing people to upgrade gear. There are some missions, like twilight missions (harder versions of main missions) that will activate these players when you get in range no matter if you want to fight them or not. There is also an enemy that will summon any remnants as well as other baddies until you kill it.

Dojo: Some skills and abilities are gated through the Dojo, which serves as a teaching center for your abilities. These start out really easy and unlock as you progress through the story. There are some where you use your own gear, skills, items and abilities and others where you are locked to a wooden weapon and basic gear with limited healing items and/or useables. This is a one on one battle where you have to prove your skills. I have passed every mission in the dojo to where I am now. They aren't easy. They require you to show you can play the game. After these you unlock the abilities that help make the game easier.

Gear: Diablo. The loot system is amazing. Outside of the remnants for gear you can also forge, reforge (change stats), dismantle, and even level up existing gear to higher levels and even ability inherit traits from other items. There are items that are usable, gear that you can wear, and consumables such as ammo you can pick up from killing baddies and looting chests. There are hidden rooms and path ways. It makes for a very rich experience with the ability to form gear to your play style.

Leveling up: You can level up once you beat the tutorial mission and reach the first shrine on the island where you start. You gain Amrita which allows you level up your characters stats. These stats unlock skill points for the varying skill system which I will discuss below. Other attributes give you health or Ki, weapon dmg, or ninja abilities and magic power. Certain attributes effect the dmg of specific weapons. When you start the game you will be asked to chose 2 weapons and a guardian spirit. The options for the weapons are not really meaningful, but the guardian spirit does matter as it will be with you until you unlock the others.

Guardian Spirits: These are spirits that follow you and feed off your amrita. When they are full you can unleash them for a short period of time enhancing your skills based on the spirit you have. You take dmg during the time period but it will deplete the time you have the spirit active. You can also use a talisman to cast them to do an attack which varies as well by the guardian you have active. These can be switched at your shrines and will have to be fed again with amrita by killing people or using stones to make them usable again. They give passive buffs as well when they are not being used. Think of them as your ultimate to kill a boss once you have them down to a certain percent of life.

Skill System: Weapons, Ninjitsu (Ninja Stars /Bombs) and Magic (Enchants / Ranged Spells) You will unlock skill points through missions, items and leveling up certain attributes. There are multiple weapons in the game and each type has a skill tree. These weapon skill trees have abilities that are shared among all the weapon skills. Unlocking one weapons ability will unlock it for all others. Some weapon abilities, including your passives, are not shared and require you to spend points in the specific tree to get them. Passives are shared no matter what weapons you have equipped. These use Samurai Skill points. Ninjitsu is basically your ninja stars, bombs, poison and sneak attack stuff. Magic or Onmyo is your weapon enchants, buffs, debuffs, and passives for resistance.

Combat: Ki - The Stamina of the Nioh world. The combat in the game centers around your Ki and your enemies. Attacks against you or an enemy will deplete your Ki. When you have no ki or an enemy has no ki you are staggered and can't attack for a short period. You, as well as an enemy, are open for a final blow attack or grapple depending on health remaining. The attacks you make as well as your enemies, will take ki as well. Depending on which stance will depend on how much you spend putting out damage as well as how much you ki damage you take when you are hit. You have ranged attacks with a bow, rifle and cannon. You can expand these ammo capacity through ninjitsu upgrades as well as upgrading the damage they can do.

Replayability: Season Pass DLC includes 3 story missions and maybe a new region. There is free DLC coming to add hard missions and pvp. There is a NG+ where you have to fight 2 bosses at once and even crazier shit. The gear gets better with even more options for customizing opening up.

Sound and Music:
The best sound track in a game I have heard in a very very very long time. I don't play games with much audio. I know it is odd. I don't play online games with any audio but voice chat. I had the music on and the game volume on default the entire game I have played thus far. Zelda might be the last time I enjoyed game music and sound.

Graphics: I played on a PS4 Pro. I played in movie mode and it was amazing. I didn't really notice what others had said about framerate not keeping at 30 FPS, but again I don't have counter on screen. I didn't have any issues with pop ins or hanging during combat. It was fluid. The PS4 original did have some of those issues on that mode but they recommend to use action mode with a variable frame rate and resolution.

Scoring and Final Thoughts: Sound: 4 out of 5 Music: 5 out of 5 Graphics: 4 out of 5 (PS4 Pro 5 out 5) Game play: 5 out of 5 Replayability: 5 out of 5

Score: 92 out of 100

Final Thoughts: Buy this game. If you were wondering if it was worth buying I hope that after you have read through the review you are tempted to buy it even more. The DLC is worth the 25 bucks and the game takes a while to complete for most. It has been the best money to time spent playing ratio of any game I have outside of an MMO. It is like Team Ninja took Ninja Gaiden, Dark Souls, and Bloodborne and created a new definition of the souls genre.
Late at night, when no one else is looking, you can see the Matrix code shimmering at the edges of your vision. That, or a death ray might be killing you.
